claims.text: Stable protective-oxide formation in CrFeCoNiX alloys is governed by competition between slow-growing protective oxides and fast-growing non-protective oxides.
Cr2O3 is a slow-growing protective oxide in the relevant CrFeCoNiX systems and exposure conditions.
Al2O3 is a slow-growing protective oxide in the relevant CrFeCoNiX systems and exposure conditions.
FeO is a fast-growing non-protective oxide in the relevant CrFeCoNiX systems and exposure conditions.
NiO is a fast-growing non-protective oxide in the relevant CrFeCoNiX systems and exposure conditions.
Minor alloying additions such as Ti or Y influence protective-oxide formation and growth.
Grain-boundary structure influences protective-oxide formation and growth.
Grain-boundary composition influences protective-oxide formation and growth.
Systematically varying X and minor alloying additions can modulate oxide-layer composition.
Systematically varying X and minor alloying additions can modulate oxide-layer microstructure.
The proposed intervention can produce a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layer.
The resulting protective oxide layer will persist above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere.
Formation of the proposed protective layer will improve environmental stability.
Formation of the proposed protective layer will improve structural integrity.
The proposed mechanism applies broadly to CrFeCoNiX alloys having varying compositions and microstructures.

contradictions.description: The test conditions and stated applicability are limited to exposure at 900 °C, whereas the predicted outcome claims persistence above 900 °C. A test conducted only at 900 °C cannot directly establish persistence above that temperature.
